concepts.def: Force per unit area, in N/m² or pascals.
Surface that force is spread over.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pressure = force divided by the area it's spread over.

Push a thumb on a drawing pin: same force, but the pin tip has a tiny area - huge pressure! That's why it sinks into the wood.

Sharp = small area = high pressure. Blunt = large area = low pressure.

Snowshoes spread your weight over a big area - low pressure stops you sinking.

Stiletto heels focus weight on a tiny area - high pressure dents floors!

Knives are sharp for high pressure to cut. Camels have wide feet for low pressure on sand.

Density = how much mass is packed into a volume.

Formula: density = mass ÷ volume.

Lead is dense - lots of mass in a small lump.
Foam is not dense - small mass in a big lump.

Water has a density of 1 g/cm³.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the motor effect and electromagnetic induction?
options: The motor effect only works on DC; induction only works on AC.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
The motor effect produces a force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field; induction produces an emf when flux linkage changes.
They are the same phenomenon described in different words.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.
The motor effect only works on DC; induction only works on AC.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.

mcqs.q: What does specific latent heat measure?
options: The energy required to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature.
The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg by 1 degree.
The motor effect only works on DC; induction only works on AC.
The temperature at which a substance melts or boils.
